summary: Cajeme municipal cadastral stewardship and official Ciudad Obregón value-map publications were evidenced, along with the ICReson Cajeme registry office, but no anonymous first-party parcel geometry service with safe native IDs was verified. No sample GeoJSON was retained.
queryOutcomes: English and Spanish discovery queries are recorded verbatim in city-1983-ciudad-obreg-n.json. Results identified local/state cadastral custodians and official value-map/procedure pages, not an open parcel API.
requestOutcomes: The municipal application landing page, municipal deslinde procedure, official Sonora cadastral value-map PDFs, and ICReson office page were checked. No login, CAPTCHA bypass, credentials, private token, unsafe field, or TLS verification bypass was used.
scopeLimits: Cajeme value-map PDFs are official published cadastral products but are not machine-readable parcel geometry responses.
The municipal deslinde page documents a request workflow requiring title/deed material; it is not evidence of an anonymous parcel API.
ICReson confirms the state registry office for Cajeme/ Ciudad Obregón but does not expose a public parcel layer in the inspected page.
No exact-point hit, map extent miss, timeout, unavailable UI, or absent endpoint was treated as evidence of citywide parcel absence.

geometryRetention.reason: No safe, verified native parcel geometry response was available.

uncertainty: Open parcel coverage, schema, CRS, native identity semantics, and citywide completeness remain unverified. Local cadastral stewardship is documented, but public geometry access and runtime integration are not admitted.
